title: Blue Jays reportedly agree to deal with speedy infielder/outfielder Jazz Chisholm Jr.

blocks.text: It appears the Toronto Blue Jays have reached a contract agreement with Jazz Chisholm Jr., the former New York Yankees infielder who hit .231 this past season with 19 home runs and career-high 41 stolen bases for the New York Yankees.
Former Yankee stole 41 bases this past season and hit 31 homers in 2025

Infielder/outfielder Jazz Chisholm Jr. and the Toronto Blue Jays have agreed to a contract guaranteeing $34.5 million US over two seasons, two people familiar with the negotiations told The Associated Press.
Sportsnet, ESPN and New York Post also are reporting the two sides have agreed on a deal. ESPN says it's a one-year contract worth $20 million US.
The Blue Jays have yet to confirm the signing.

A two-time all-star, Chisholm gets a $6 million signing bonus and a $12.5 million salary next season. The deal includes a $16 million player option for 2028 and if that option is declined, Toronto has a $40 million club option with a $1.5 million buyout.
Chisholm hit .231 with 19 homers and 55 runs batted in with a career-high 41 stolen bases for the New York Yankees last season.
The 28-year-old, who made his major league debut with the Miami Marlins in 2020, hit 31 homers and drove in 80 runs for the Yankees in 2025.

blocks.text: The Blue Jays are coming off a last-place finish in the American League East this past season after reaching the World Series in 2025.

Chisholm gives Blue Jays a left-handed bat with some pop, along with some speed and defensive versatility. Chisholm has struggled with errors at times, but he can also play shortstop, third base and outfield if needed.

Second baseman Ernie Clement may shift back to a utilityman role after enduring a poor second half. Clement was an all-star this past season but couldn't seem to shake a long slump after his strong start to the campaign.
